Jordan —

Quick summary from Finance: we cannot permanently remove invoice ledger entries that are required for tax and audit compliance. For the US, typical retention is 6–7 years depending on state and transaction type.

Options to propose to the customer:
- We can permanently delete application-level usage logs and any PII in telemetry tied to the user,
- We can retain billing ledger entries in our accounting system (immutable entries) but provide redacted invoice PDFs that remove bill-to PII, or provide a certified export of invoice data to the customer,
- If BrightBridge requires full erasure of invoice content, we can offer an exception evaluation with Legal to see if a statutory retention waiver applies (rare).

If we provide redacted invoices, we should include a notarized statement or a signed letter indicating we are retaining ledger records for compliance. For this thread I attached an example of a redacted invoice template to show what we can deliver.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Manager, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

On 2027-04-18 14:45, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Subject: Re: Fwd: Please delete our account and associated data

Jordan / Neha —

Legal concurs with Finance: accounting records (invoices, ledger entries) are subject to retention obligations. Key points for the customer response:
- We can delete user-level content and telemetry that is not required for billing or legal hold.
- Invoice documents may contain PII; we can provide redacted copies and a formal statement that immutable accounting entries are preserved solely for statutory compliance.
- If BrightBridge insists on absolute erasure of invoice content, escalate to Compliance for a written exception review; this typically requires a commercial negotiation and internal sign-offs (Finance + Legal + Compliance).

Also check the SOW/contract for any express invoicing retention clauses — some customers agreed to specific record-keeping terms. If BrightBridge has such a clause we need to quote it in our reply.

-Marissa
General Counsel (interim)
Redwood Inference
